children: , the world's largest contract chipmaker, is setting up an advanced-packaging testing and training hub in Kaohsiung. Its U.S. shares rose about 0.4% to $453.02 around 10:28 a.m. ET Friday, based on Thursday's $451.15 close.

The plan gives suppliers a place to test equipment and materials alongside TSMC before those technologies reach production. Two buildings are expected to open in late 2029. TSMC has said the setup could make validation 25% to 50% more efficienta useful gain if demand for complex AI chips keeps climbing.

Here's the catch for investors: faster testing is not the same as more chips ready to sell. The picture puts the shares 24.45% above GuruFocus's $364.01 GF Value estimate. That premium raises the bar for TSMC to turn better supplier coordination into real manufacturing gains.

title: TSMC Stocks Rise as Packaging Moves Closer to Suppliers
